fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. Matthew says, “…He withdrew to Galilee.” (Matthew 4:12) John, the man who baptized Jesus (Matthew 3:13), has been put in prison, and Jesus heads for Galilee. The text doesn't tell us why, so I won't make something up. I'll just say it's a quiet move, and the big stuff starts right after.

Close, but that's already behind Him, baker. The Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness, where He fasted forty days and forty nights (Matthew 4:1-2). This time, Matthew says He withdrew to Galilee. Jesus keeps moving forward.

Capernaum, yes! Matthew says Jesus went and lived there, by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali. Notice that He doesn't just pass through. He moves in. A fresh town, a fresh start, nothing like the junk drawer I got shoved into for years.

Tyre is a real name, friend, but Matthew doesn't use it here. He says Jesus left Nazareth and went and lived in Capernaum, by the sea in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali. I mix up my own cookie shapes all the time, so no shame in grabbing the wrong town. Capernaum is the one to keep on your counter.

Light, baker! Isaiah, the prophet, said, “…the people living in darkness have seen a great light…” (Matthew 4:16) Matthew says Jesus moving to Capernaum fulfills those words (Matthew 4:13-14). I know a little about living in the dark, and when the light finally showed up in my life, I felt it.

At once is right, friend. Matthew says, “And at once they left their nets and followed Him.” Simon Peter and Andrew are fishermen, and those nets are their work. When the angel called me out of that junk drawer, I asked for one minute first. Matthew's word for these two is at once.

Zebedee, yes! Matthew says James and his brother John “…were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets.” Three of them, one boat, and nets to mend. The text puts them all together right there.

Nathanael is a good name, baker, but Matthew doesn't put him in this boat. He says James and John “…were in a boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets.” Zebedee is the one Matthew names with them. Nathanael isn't mentioned in these verses.
City gates make a good guess, baker. But this verse names a different spot. Jesus went throughout Galilee, “…teaching in their synagogues…” That's where Matthew says He taught.

You got it, baker! Matthew says Jesus was “…healing every disease and sickness among the people.” Every one. He's teaching, preaching and healing, all in the same trip through Galilee. That's a lot of ground to cover, and I'm tired just reading it.
